n: The topic of this lecture: cocaine and cocaine-containing preparations, their isolation from biological fluids and analysis. The outline: the history and plant of coca, types of preparation, action, toxicokinetics, production, and colour and chromatographic analysis. Key words: ecgonine, benzoylecgonine, cocaine paste, crack, the Scott reaction, TLC and HPLC.

The Indians of South America have used the leaves of the coca shrub for 5000 years, in religious rites and to reduce the sensation of fatigue and hunger. Cocaine was isolated from coca leaf in 1859 at the University of Göttingen by Albert Niemann, and was synthesised in 1902. In the 18th-19th centuries cocaine, as a harmless stimulant and painkiller, was included in medicines, drinks, wine and sweets.

In 1886 the pharmacist John Pemberton produced the drink Coca-Cola with cocaine added. Because the drink caused dependence, it was banned by the US government in 1904, and from 1914 measures began to be taken in other countries as well. In 1961 the international Convention on Narcotic Drugs control was adopted, and under it cocaine is prohibited. The diagram shows the sequence of these years: 1859, 1886, 1902, 1904, 1914 and 1961.

The coca shrub's homeland is Peru and Bolivia; at present it is not found in the wild at all. It has been cultivated since antiquity: first by the Indians, and in the 20th century plantations were set up on the islands of Java and Sri Lanka, in South-East Asia, and later in Africa. In the Erythroxylon family 200 species are known, and 17 species accumulate cocaine. Because of the high cocaine content, only Erythroxylon coca and E. novogranatense are grown.

Coca leaves contain various alkaloids in an amount of 0.5-1.5%, the main one being cocaine; its share makes up 30% of the total alkaloids. The rest are ecgonine derivatives: methylecgonine, cis- and trans-cinnamoylcocaine, benzoylecgonine, tropacocaine and truxillic acid. All the derivatives of ecgonine are used in industry for the semisynthesis of cocaine. Hygrine and cuscohygrine are also found in the leaves.

Coca leaves are used to prepare Coca mate tea, distributed on the black market; it is a mild stimulant compared with coffee. Cocaine paste, that is cocaine sulphate, is found under the names basuco, basa, pitillo and testo, and is regarded as a low-grade narcotic drug. The paste is widespread in South America among the poorer sections of the population. Remember: it is an intermediate product in processing coca leaf.

We classify cocaine preparations. Coca leaf, that is Coca mate tea, and cocaine paste, that is cocaine sulphate, are intermediate and low-grade products. Cocaine hydrochloride, powder or rock, and cocaine base, that is crack or freebase, are the main finished forms. Disguises and mixtures: brown cocaine, which contains 40% cocaine, black cocaine, with a polymer, and speedball, with heroin added.

Coca and cocaine in figures. In the Erythroxylon family 200 species are known, 17 species accumulate cocaine, and a large amount of cocaine occurs in only two species. The leaves contain 0.5-1.5% alkaloids, and cocaine makes up 30% of the total alkaloids. From leaves collected once from 1 ha, 5 kg of cocaine can be obtained.

Cocaine hydrochloride is a white crystalline powder, chow, usually odourless; it also occurs as large colourless crystals, rock. It is used for intravenous injection or to obtain cocaine base; its cocaine content is 80-90%. For street trade it is diluted by adding 12-50% of piracetam, caffeine, lidocaine, procaine, benzocaine, sugar and starch. That is, the share of cocaine in a street sample may be considerably lower.

Cocaine base is obtained from the hydrochloride and is called crack or freebase. Brown cocaine is prepared to disguise it from the addict, in the form of instant coffee or tea; it contains about 40% cocaine. Black cocaine is mixed with polymer material, from which statuettes, briefcases and holders are made. Speedball is an equal mixture of cocaine and heroin. Coca leaf and cocaine are among the strongest plant-based stimulants known to man.

Cocaine acts on the dopaminergic system of the human brain. The early signs are emotional excitement, strength and energy, an acceleration of mental activity, reduced tendency to sleep, loss of appetite and loss of weight. Reddening of the skin from the bites of cocaine bugs, dilated pupils, indistinct speech, tremor, insomnia and a chronic runny nose are also seen.

We consider the severe effects by system. On the neuropsychiatric side, convulsions, spasms, depression, delirium, false and irrational ideas and hallucinations are seen. In the respiratory system, difficulty in breathing, pulmonary oedema and respiratory arrest are possible. In the cardiovascular system there are arrhythmia, infarction, cardiac arrest, cerebral infarction and stroke; a tendency to suicide has also been recorded.

The half-life differs by substance. For cocaine it is 38-67 minutes, for benzoylecgonine 4-6 hours, and for methylecgonine 2.5-7.6 hours. That is, cocaine is measured in minutes and its metabolites in hours. Benzoylecgonine and methylecgonine persist longer than cocaine, so metabolites are important in analysis.

The bioavailability of cocaine depends on the route of administration. Taken by mouth or through the nose it is 20-40%, and smoked 6-32%. When injected into a vein, bioavailability is 100%. Thus, the more direct the route of administration, the higher the proportion of cocaine that enters the blood.

Doses of cocaine. The clinical dose is 1.5 mg/kg; the lethal dose for a person who has not taken it before is 200 mg. A single street dose is 15-60 mg. For administration into the nose, a line, 3-5 cm long, an amount of 10-20 mg to 50-100 mg is used.

Taken by mouth, the toxic dose is 500 mg and the lethal dose is 1.2 g. In individual cases the lethal dose may fall to 20 mg or rise to 8-10 g. The book also gives the lethal dose for a person who has not taken it before as 200 mg. These differences show a dependence on the individual sensitivity of the organism.

Excretion and metabolites. 90-95% of a single dose is excreted in the urine over 2-3 days. Excretion is mainly as metabolites; norcocaine and hydroxylated metabolites are up to 10%. The shares in urine: cocaine 1-9%, benzoylecgonine 35-60%, methylecgonine 32-49%, ecgonine 1-8%.

t: Detection time in urine and special signs
n: Detection time in urine. After a single dose, unchanged cocaine is detected in urine for 8-24 hours, and as benzoylecgonine and methylecgonine for 48 hours. With chronic use, the detection time extends to 5 days. There are also special signs: if the ethyl ester of benzoylecgonine is found in urine, cocaine and alcohol were taken at the same time. If the methyl ester of anhydroecgonine is found, crack, that is cocaine base, was smoked.

Stages in obtaining cocaine paste. Finely chopped leaves are mixed with solutions of water and lime, that is potash, and steeped. The leaves are extracted with kerosene, and then the extract is re-extracted with acidified water. The aqueous part is made alkaline with lime and ammonia: crude cocaine precipitates and is dried, and the paste results.

Obtaining cocaine base and hydrochloride from the paste. The paste is dissolved in dilute sulphuric acid, and KMnO4 solution is added until a pink colour forms. After several days it is filtered, the filtrate is made alkaline with ammonia, and the precipitate is cocaine base. The purified base is dissolved in ether, and concentrated HCl and acetone are added, whereupon cocaine hydrochloride precipitates.

Reagent consumption in production. For 100 kg of cocaine hydrochloride, 100-400 l of sulphuric acid, 20 kg of potassium permanganate and 30 l of hydrochloric acid are used. In addition, 1500-2000 l of acetone, or diethyl ether, or methyl ethyl ketone, or toluene are consumed. According to the data, 5 kg of cocaine can be obtained from coca leaves collected once from 1 ha.

t: Precursors: their role in cocaine production
n: In the precursor list, acetone, methyl ethyl ketone, toluene and diethyl ether are listed as solvents. Sulphuric and hydrochloric acids are listed as reagents, as they are used in preparing many narcotic drugs. Acetone is listed as a solvent in preparing pervitin, LSD, cocaine, heroin and others. This is reflected in Table 18.

We summarise the reagents in cocaine production by stage. First stage, paste: water and lime, that is potash, kerosene and ammonia. Second stage, cocaine base: dilute H2SO4, KMnO4 and ammonia. Third stage, hydrochloride: ether, concentrated HCl and acetone. At each stage the reagents change, and the product is purified successively.

We compare the reactions in cocaine analysis. Mayer and Dragendorff reagents and picric acid give an amorphous precipitate. KMnO4 and HCl give red-violet crystals. The Scott reaction, that is cobalt thiocyanate, gives a blue colour. Hydrolysis and ethyl alcohol give the smell of ethyl benzoate. In the pharmacological test, the pupil dilates in a cat's eye and sensation on the tip of the tongue is reduced.

Isolation from biological fluids. Cocaine is extracted well with chloroform from blood, urine and other biological fluids in an alkaline medium, at pH 7.0-8.5. It is also partly extracted in an acid medium. A small volume of the extract is taken, the solvent is evaporated, and the residue is dissolved in hydrochloric acid. The reactions are carried out with this solution.

With Mayer, Bouchardat and Dragendorff reagents and picric acid, cocaine forms mainly amorphous precipitates. In the presence of potassium permanganate and hydrochloric acid, cocaine forms red-violet crystals of rectangular shape. Both reactions are carried out with a sample obtained from the extract and dissolved in hydrochloric acid. The microcrystalline reaction gives a more definite result than the precipitation reaction.

The Scott reaction. The reagent consists of a 1:1 mixture of a 2% solution of cobalt thiocyanate and 96% glycerol; 5 drops are added to the sample. If cocaine is present, a blue colour forms. 1-2 drops of concentrated HCl discharge the colour. Then, when a few drops of chloroform are added, it is stained dark blue.

Hydrolysis, smell and pharmacological tests. The aqueous extract is hydrolysed with 2 drops of concentrated HCl and ethyl alcohol is added: the characteristic smell of ethyl benzoate appears. In identification by smell, dry material is moistened with a solution of KOH in methanol, and after the excess alcohol evaporates, the smell is compared with a standard sample. In the pharmacological method, when a cocaine solution is instilled into one eye of a cat, the pupil dilates. Cocaine powder is also identified by the reduced sensation on the tip of the tongue.

For TLC, Sorbton, Sorbfil or Kieselgel G 60 plates are used as the stationary phase. The results for cocaine and its metabolites, as Rf100, are given in Table 3. There are three solvent systems. The first is chloroform:dioxane:EtOAc:NH3 25:60:10:5. The second is methanol:25% ammonia 100:1.5. The third is cyclohexane:toluene:diethylamine 75:15:10.

In the first system, cocaine gives 81, cinnamoylcocaine 83, benzocaine 77 and methadone 75, that is, the Rf100 values are close to one another. Procaine is 61. The values change with the system: for cocaine 81, 59 and 56. The book gives three solvent systems for cocaine. Because of the close values, relying on a single system is not sufficient.

TLC results: cocaine and its metabolites. Cocaine gives a definite value in all three systems: 81, 59 and 56. Ecgonine 0, 84 and 0, methylecgonine 61, 65 and 44, benzoylecgonine 0, 25 and 0. Ecgonine and benzoylecgonine stay on the starting line in the first and third systems, that is Rf100 = 0.

The Rf100 values of additives and methadone in the first, second and third systems. Cinnamoylcocaine 83, 59, 51. Benzocaine 77, 80, 11. Methadone 75, 41, 74. Procaine 61, 55, 10. These substances are included in the table for comparison with cocaine; benzocaine and procaine are also shown as substances added to cocaine preparations.

The HPLC method. The analysis is carried out on a Milichrom 4 chromatograph, with a KAKh-4 column, 62x2 mm. The eluent is a mixture of phosphate buffer and acetonitrile in the ratio 80:20, with an elution rate of 100 µl/min. The detection wavelengths are 210, 234, 254, 276 and 302 nm.

The stages of UV spectrophotometric quantitative analysis. An exact weighed portion of 10-15 mg is taken from the sample and dissolved in 50 ml of purified water; the water is acidified with 2-3 drops of concentrated HCl. From the solution obtained, 5 ml is placed in a 50 ml volumetric flask and made up to the mark with purified water. From the UV spectrum the absorbance at 234 nm is determined, and the concentration of cocaine hydrochloride is found from the calibration line. The quantity of cocaine in the sample is stated and the report is drawn up.

The general scheme of analysis is as follows. First, isolation with chloroform is carried out in an alkaline medium, at pH 7.0-8.5, and the residue is dissolved in hydrochloric acid. At the preliminary stage, precipitating reagents, KMnO4 microcrystals and the Scott reaction are applied. For confirmation and quantification, TLC, Rf100, HPLC and UV spectrophotometry, 234 nm, are used. Finally, the report is drawn up.

In urine screening, the cutoff for cocaine is 300 ng/ml, and in confirmation 150 ng/ml for benzoylecgonine. Cocaine is detected in urine 2-6 hours after intake and, after a single intake, may be detectable for 48-72 hours. According to the book, unchanged cocaine is detected for 8-24 hours and its metabolites for 48 hours. The difference between sources is related to the type of data.

Practical case. Urine was brought to the forensic chemical examination as the biological specimen; when the extract was analysed by GC-MS, cocaethylene was found. Task: explain the analytical result and fill in the problem table, that is write the type of problem, the causes of its origin and the ways to resolve it. Remember: the ethyl ester of benzoylecgonine in urine indicates that cocaine and alcohol were taken together.

To conclude. Cocaine is the main alkaloid of coca leaf, 30% of the total alkaloids; its preparations are paste, hydrochloride and base, that is crack. In urine, mainly metabolites are found: benzoylecgonine 35-60%, methylecgonine 32-49%. The analysis is carried out by isolation with chloroform at pH 7.0-8.5, the Scott and KMnO4 reactions, TLC, HPLC and UV-SP, 234 nm. Review questions: from which plant and how is cocaine isolated; its metabolites; microcrystalline reactions; distinguishing it from cadaveric alkaloids.
